reason: The PR adds a TSPFix local-search operator to both CVRP and VRPTW search and calls it for suitable multi-job routes. This expands the neighborhood and can change incumbent quality and search cost on actual solver workloads.
solver_behavior_hypothesis: A route-level TSP optimization move may improve incumbents on routes with enough jobs, while its candidate checks and TSP subsolves may consume time that could be spent on other neighborhoods.
causal_chain: The new local-search branch constructs TSPFix for eligible same-route candidates without shipments, compares its gain with existing moves, and can accept it as the best operator. This may reorder route jobs and redirect subsequent search.
structural_trigger: CVRP or VRPTW instances with non-shipment routes of at least two jobs that satisfy the solver's good-TSP-candidate condition; short routes or shipment requests are controls.
activation_probe: Count eligible routes, TSPFix constructions, valid positive-gain moves, accepted TSPFix moves, and route-cost trajectories in paired pinned builds; record inactive controls.
instance_selection_rule: Freeze routing instances by route length, customer count, shipment presence, and time-window structure before hidden scoring; retain the selected nontriggering controls, seeds, and all timeouts.
workload_exposure_plan: Use the shared VROOM solver driver and independent original-instance route verifier, then trace the TSPFix branch on public CVRP cases before qualifying a hidden task. A build or title alone is insufficient.
mathematical_risk: A TSPFix gain or route rewrite can violate capacity, time windows, pickup-delivery ordering, or objective accounting and may hide a better move; returned routes must be checked against original requests.
independent_check_plan: Independently verify every route, job assignment, capacity, and objective on original instances, with targeted small-route tests comparing TSPFix gain against exact route cost.
hidden_generalization_plan: Report verified incumbent quality, time-to-target, and family-level regressions on held-out CVRP and time-window routing instances at paired budgets and seeds.
overlap_review: This 2023 neighborhood addition is distinct from #1222's 2025 insertion-bound pruning, but each historical PR counts once despite separate CVRP and VRPTW implementations.
resource_risk: The extra route-level TSP search can add CPU and temporary memory for long routes without improving the final incumbent on every family.
